name: Play Families policy and Apple Kids category
plain: Child directed apps get stricter rules: no ads tracking, no personal data to third parties, and certified SDKs.
meaning: Apple's Kids category bans behavioral ads and limits third-party analytics. Play Families requires certified ad SDKs, no AAID use, and a safe design. Both align with COPPA and similar laws.

android.store_policy: Families policy: no AAID or sensitive identifiers; Play Families Self-Certified Ads SDK program; target audience declaration
android.api_surface: Play Console > Target audience and content
android.note: Apps targeting children cannot send AAID to third parties.

ios.store_policy: Guideline 1.3 Kids Category and 5.1.4: no third-party analytics or ads with identifiers; parental gate for links and purchases
ios.api_surface: App Store Connect > Kids category, parental gate
ios.note: Parental gate required for external links.

limits.headline: Can't track children or share their data with ad companies in kids apps
limits.user_action: Nothing. The rules apply when a child uses a kids category or Families app
can: Show ads from certified ad tools only (Android)
Collect the data the app needs to work
Ask a parent for permission before outside links (iPhone parental gate)
cannot: Send the Google advertising ID to third parties for a child directed app
Use behavioral ads or most outside analytics in the Apple Kids category
Send personal data to third parties without the rules allowing it
Open outside links without a parental gate (iPhone)
limits.differs: Apple has the Kids category with a parental gate. Google Play Families requires certified ad tools and no ad ID use.

story.what_it_is: Stricter store rules for apps made for children, with no ad tracking and certified tools.

marketing.name: Families policy
marketing.pitch: Apps for children must use certified ad SDKs, skip the advertising ID and follow safe design.

marketing.name: Kids Category
marketing.pitch: Apps in the Kids category must not include behavioral ads or send data to third parties.

story.for_you: Your child sees fewer and gentler ads, and apps are not allowed to follow them around. Parental gates guard buying and links.
story.for_makers: Kids apps still earn through approved ad networks and subscriptions. Makers must pick certified SDKs and ship a parent gate, or the app is removed.

use_cases.example: A children's puzzle game shows only contextual ads that do not use a profile.
A reading app uses no third party analytics, only its own safe data.
A kids video app puts a parent gate (a math question) before any link to the web or store.
An ad network certifies its SDK to run in kids apps with no advertising ID.
A drawing app saves art only on the device and never uploads a child's photo.
A game maker removes a data SDK that was not certified and is flagged in review.

story.android_note: Play Families requires certified ad SDKs and bars the advertising ID.
story.ios_note: Apple's Kids Category bans behavioral ads and limits third party analytics.

technical_bounds: Mixed audience apps have special rules

history.change: Families policy tightened on ad SDK certification
